family_judgments.evidence: Every format measures the same MIGHT-plus-miss expression of possible failure to catch the train.
Recognition and production mechanisms differ, but the grammatical target remains unchanged.
All items retain the delayed journey and possible missed train meaning.

criteria.evidence: “Might miss” directly requires central MIGHT with its base-form complement.
The frame fixes first person, object, and time reference without requiring another major operation.
Use of both specified words requires the declared construction.
The constrained blank has the single normal response “might miss.”
Neither solver supplied a reasonable unkeyed alternative.
Traffic, train, and miss are context-supported and appropriate for B2.
The reply must express uncertainty through “might miss.”
The dialogue does not demand an additional grammatical conversion.
The specified words and blank require the target modal construction.
“Might miss” is the determinate completion under the instruction.
No reasonable unkeyed response was proposed by the automated attempts.
The ten-minute departure context makes the intended meaning readily inferable.
The target is represented, but learners can select A by eliminating the three overtly nonstandard complement forms.
The options differ only in forms licensed after MIGHT.
Recognition can be achieved through distractor elimination rather than affirmative deployment of the modal rule.
Only A is a grammatical MIGHT-plus-base-form sentence.
The single correct option A is accepted.
No difficult lexical or discourse inference is needed to distinguish the options.
The mandated “might” and “miss” require the central-modal/base-complement sequence.
The learner must recast an existential possibility clause as a first-person declarative.
The required modal and lexical verb preclude a target-avoiding keyed answer.
The fixed pronoun, verb, object, and time anchor support the keyed response uniquely.
No reasonable unkeyed alternative was identified by the solver attempts.
Paraphrasing “There is a possibility that...” introduces modest non-target transformation demand.

summary: Acceptable MIGHT family. Its MCQ is somewhat susceptible to elimination and the transformation has modest paraphrase burden, but the construct remains aligned.
